reason: Repeated ஆலயமாக for syllables and subtle form pairs closely with உள்ளம் பெருங்கோயில் and ஊனுடம்பு ஆலயம்.
ஐம்புலன் கட்டுண்ணும் வீடு and guarding ஐவாய வேட்கை to gain வீடு tie restraint to release in both verses.
The thirty-six match, but the ladder stanza does not make a guru’s teaching a prerequisite for ascending it.
The first puts one letter above fifty; it does not connect that one to the five of the second or describe an intervening five-letter stage.
A list of sounds perceived by those who bow does not establish that the dawn sun as conch is an instance of its inner conch sound.
The distinctive cluster of gods, injured bodily parts, and divine action links a narrated catastrophe to a stanza interpreting those losses through Hara’s grace.
Both have தோற்பை and a crow taking the body; calling the skin bag I in the song illuminates the contrast with the dancer leaving it.
The two gods failing to know Siva are absent in the first passage, and the song’s direct plea to know and praise is addressed to the spear-bearing lord.
The sweets can be vocatives addressed to Murugan rather than descriptions of the requested experience; the qualification rests on that unresolved attachment.
எனயனத்தில் உற்று நடமிடும் and கண்ணுள்ளின் போகார் both stage the beloved inside the eye, with different actions and objects of attachment.
The song declines matted hair and bodily privation and seeks knowledge; the Kural explicitly makes shaving or growing hair unnecessary given good conduct.
The punctured flesh-bag and the skin covering many openings share a bodily image, whose target shifts from a desired body to the speaker’s own.
The echoed வரைத்து வலஞ்செய் question and answer connect the unbounded lord to an explicit manner of circumambulation with water, flowers and name.
The demand for பொற்பணம் before sweet speech dramatizes the Kural’s association of இன்சொல் with desire for wealth.
Both portray Murugan worshipping before the hill woman, and the first repeats தஞ்சம் in the worshipper’s request and the divine courtship.
The supplied offering verse lists flowers alone, and கன்மம் in the other is broad enough that it need not mean this offering specifically.
